correctness.rationale: Total domination in a complete multipartite graph is equivalent to meeting at least two parts. The complement induces either a connected complete multipartite graph when it meets at least two parts, or an edgeless graph with one component per vertex when it lies in one part. These two exact structural facts prove the classification, enumerator, and gamma formulas. Exhaustive replay through order 10 matched every subset and coefficient and confirmed the bipartite boundary cases.

evidence: Rad--Volkmann (2016) gives general bounds and exact values for complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs and paths, but no theorem covering arbitrary complete multipartite graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General graph bounds do not imply the exact part-profile classification or coefficient enumerator. Complete bipartite graphs are a strict subclass and their published endpoint statement is not valid at \(k=n\).

evidence: At \(k=n\) in \(K_{m,n}\), an \(n\)-component complement must be the entire size-\(n\) part, leaving \(D\) inside the other independent part; therefore \(G[D]\) has isolated vertices and \(D\) is not total dominating.
For \(K_{2,2}=C_4\) this gives \(\gamma_{tc}^2=0\), matching Theorem 2.6 of Rad--Volkmann and contradicting the endpoint reading of Proposition 3.2.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior bipartite formula does not imply the corrected result; rather, its endpoint is refuted by the defining condition. The arbitrary multipartite enumeration strictly strengthens the valid interior bipartite cases.

originality.rationale: The defining 2016 paper was inspected at statement level. It treats complete bipartite graphs only at the scalar level and its Proposition 3.2 includes the endpoint \(k=n\); the new claim gives an arbitrary complete-multipartite all-set classification and bivariate enumerator and proves that the bipartite endpoint is infeasible. The endpoint correction is forced by the total-domination condition and is consistent with the same paper’s Theorem 2.6 for \(C_4\). Targeted semantic and literature searches found no later correction or dominating arbitrary-multipartite statement.
residual_risks: An obscure later correction or equivalent result under substantially different terminology could be poorly indexed; no such source was surfaced by the targeted searches.

source_inspections.assessment: Defines TOkCDS; gives a complete-bipartite scalar formula with a non-strict endpoint \(k=n\) and separately states \(\gamma_{tc}^2(C_4)=0\). It contains no arbitrary complete-multipartite all-set enumerator.
source_inspections.evidence: Definition requires \(D\) to be total dominating and \(G[V-D]\) to have exactly \(k\) components; Proposition 3.2 prints \(m+n-k\) for \(2\le k\le n\), while Theorem 2.6 lists \(C_4\) among graphs with \(\gamma_{tc}^2=0\).

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for the parameter introduced in the source paper, not an arbitrary slice. It both resolves an internal endpoint conflict in a published exact formula and supplies the missing arbitrary complete-multipartite all-set enumerator. The correction changes feasibility at the largest \(k\) in every nontrivial complete bipartite graph, while the \(r\ge3\) case shows why the endpoint becomes feasible again.
